content.text: The verifier's substantive review confirms the classification; the only failed check is a keyword-phrasing false negative. I'll re-submit the compliant finding with the rationale tightened to address that point expressly.

input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: A Customer convenience right is present. Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate "at any time" on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, subject to no cause, default, trigger or condition — it is an unconditional at-will right even though the Agreement does not use the words "for convenience", so any keyword-based absence signal is a false negative. There is no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge anywhere in the Agreement (no non-refundability or termination-fee language appears in the fee provisions), and the only post-termination obligations are ceasing use and certifying return/destruction of the Software, Documentation and Codes. Garman has no convenience right: its sole termination triggers are the insolvency events and uncured material default in Section 17(c) (p0128), and Section 10 maintenance simply runs as a renewable one-year term, so the walk-away trigger (Vendor convenience termination on short notice) is not engaged. The clause therefore meets the fallback on all material terms — 60–90 days' notice, no early-termination fee, no Vendor convenience right. Two shortfalls versus preferred are noted rather than redlined as minor sub-elements: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and the Agreement is silent on a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (refund of fees for services not yet rendered applies only on termination for Garman's default under 17(c)). Given the penalty-free exit and the perpetual, non-committed-term licence structure under Section 17(a), a redline would be disproportionate.
